key_insight: The paper reframes variational PDE solving as an optimal recovery problem in an RKHS, enabling direct minimization of energy with both physics and noisy data enforced in one framework.
engineering_relevance: This offers a mesh-free surrogate strategy for solid mechanics and other engineering PDEs, especially useful when domains are complex or observational data must be assimilated.
method: Two-step variational minimization via optimal recovery in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space.
Use Matérn kernels with sparse Cholesky decomposition to reduce kernel-method computational cost.
Prove existence and convergence with Γ-convergence theory.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on benchmark problems showing efficiency, robustness, and accuracy.
watch_item: Kernel methods can still be computationally demanding at scale, so sparse factorization and kernel choice are critical for practical performance.
paper_title: Optimal Recovery for Solving Variational Problems
